title: Multi-Partner Project: Artificial Intelligence in Manufacturing Leading to Sustainability and the Consideration of Human Aspects (AIMS5.0)
problem: Industry 5.0 requires convergence of sustainability, digital autonomy, and human-centric design; translating these principles into practical hardware and tool implementations is challenging.
motivation: Industrial transformation toward Industry 5.0 demands integration of AI-driven hardware, tools, and methodologies that balance efficiency, innovation, and human factors.
method: By connecting academic AI researchers directly with manufacturers, the project grounds AI solutions in real factory problems rather than lab settings. The resulting AI-driven tools and hardware are designed with two constraints built in from the start: they must keep humans meaningfully involved in decisions (not just executing automated steps), and they must reduce environmental impact. This co-design approach means technical capability and human/sustainability requirements shape each other.
key_novelty: Industry 5.0 AI systems can integrate automation hardware, digital autonomy (system flexibility and independence), environmental sustainability, and human involvement as mutually reinforcing rather than competing priorities.
contributions: AI-driven hardware and tool chain development for manufacturing
Methodologies addressing human aspects in industrial automation
Bridge between academic research and practical industrial deployment
limitations: Not discussed; project overview focuses on vision rather than specific technical results.
primary_theme: AI and hardware for sustainable Industry 5.0
